profileText: a Delegate from Virginia; born at "Bathurst," near Dunnsville, Essex County, Va., in 1730; completed preparatory studies; signed the Westmoreland Association in 1766; member of Essex committee on safety in 1774; member of the Virginia house of burgesses in 1774 and 1775; delegate to the Revolutionary conventions of 1775 and 1776; member of the Virginia state house of delegates, 1776-1778; Delegate to the Second Continental Congress, 1778-1779; Delegate to the Confederation Congress, 1781; again a member of the Virginia state house of delegates in 1781, 1782, 1785, and 1788; delegate to the Virginia state ratification convention in 1788; died at "Marigold," near Ozeana, Essex County, Va., January 25, 1790; interment on his estate at "Bathurst," near Dunnsville, Essex County, Va.

researchRecord.name: In the Miscellaneous Manuscripts Collection, 1779-1792, 3 items.
researchRecord.description: One letter from Meriwether Smith was written on February 21, 1779 to John Page concerning the scarcity of provisions, depreciation of currency, potential of Virginia as a market for eastern states, and other economic and political consequences of the Revolution. The second item is from Meriwether Smith to Thomas Jefferson, Governor of Virginia, written on May 17, 1779. This letter is also signed by Richard Henry Lee and relates to the acquisition of land from Delaware Indians. The final item is a photocopy of a financial agreement between Meriwether Smith and John Beale dated January 20, 1792.
